results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Compared every independent summary with its aligned controlling idea, including attached material: all 51 units map in order to p01–p51. The summaries recover the adoption assumption and roadmap (p01–p04), model and limits (p05–p18), distinct task results and measurement lesson (p19–p23), ownership/constraints/coordination (p24–p36), standards and foundations (p37–p43), practical application (p44–p46), and synthesis/hand-off (p47–p51). The Introduction callout is retained verbatim in the outline with a null paragraph mapping: it is specified as callout evidence under p01, not an additional prose paragraph. No outline entry or flag was silently dropped.

Assessed all 52 outline entries against the draft and spec. The sole two_ideas flag is the Introduction callout, whose exact summary combines input quality and downstream constraints; those are separate bullets in the explicitly specified three-bullet overview, not two controlling ideas in a prose paragraph. All 51 aligned prose/list units retain a controlling idea. The historical quotations serve the human/tool-system idea, the qualifications in p21 serve variable task gains, and the p31/p46 lists collect examples or questions under one declared purpose.

Traced every aligned unit through its paragraph or containing-section support relationship. S1 is served by p01–p02 and p05–p18; p03–p04 connect S1 with the later claims; S2 by p19–p23 and the perception distinctions in p33–p36; S3 by p24–p36; S4 by p37–p43; S5 by p44–p46. Closing p47–p51 use their declared S1/S5, S1/S4, S3, S2/S3/S4/S5, and S3/S5 links respectively. The callout previews those same claims, and the historical lineage and optional cross-record links explain their relevance rather than introducing an orphan argument.

Audited all 47 declared evidence items and the actual six tables, four image/caption pairs, Figure 2 table/caption, examples, and quotations in the frozen draft. The pedal/guitar and arithmetic are interpreted as a model; Engelbart and Jobs are followed by human/tool-system reasoning; the limits table is followed by its surviving claim. METR, Copilot, and frontier results retain different measures and settings, and both speed tables lead to the measurement rule. The debt figures are hedged and interpreted as downstream burden; the cost table and Figure 3 are followed by the distinction between an illustration and a measured curve. Goldratt, the downstream examples and Figure 4 lead to the constraint recommendation. DORA 2024, Brooks and the conditional individual/team table explain perception, coordination and throughput; DORA 2025 quotations, foundations, Figure 5 and trust figures explain organizational conditions. The Monday table supplies reasons for its moves and is synthesized afterward. Cross-record links and the hand-off supply their relevance in the article. Image reasoning was assessed from frozen alt text/captions; external factual verification was not performed. The local wording interruptions are recorded separately under flow.

Read all 50 declared boundaries (12 container transitions and 38 within-container transitions), not only section headings. The opening moves from purchasing-story consequence to contrast and roadmap; model paragraphs express elaboration, contrast, consequence and historical support; the limits precede the example sequence; the speed cases contrast and elaborate before their measurement conclusion. Cost elaborates value, the delivery chain elaborates downstream ownership, the team gap applies constraints and adds coordination, quality picks up shared review, and organizations widen that setting. The practical table responds to the foundations, questions instantiate those moves, and the closing summarizes them, adds stage choice, and elaborates ownership through the specified next-post link. Every boundary expresses its declared relationship and carries recognizable prior material; the separate flow findings concern delayed local qualifications, not absent declared section or paragraph relationships.

Checked terminology and paragraph openings against the inherited audience. The amplifier and pedal are explained, gain is introduced as mnemonic arithmetic, task variability is defined before the frontier study, owning code is unpacked into review/testing/debugging/understanding/change, and the delivery chain and constraint are explained before their team application. Historical sources and studies receive local context; reactor, RISC and Vibe Monolith links include enough explanation of the relevant point to avoid a prerequisite reading. The personal-understanding hand-off is prepared in the ownership and Monday passages. No applicable does_not_know item remains unexplained. The change between input sign and measured-effect sign is eventually supplied but causes a reread, so that problem is recorded under flow_is_followable rather than misclassified as an entirely absent definition.

The introduction-only reader predicts all five roadmap promises in the declared order: bounded metaphor; contrasting measured and perceived task results; downstream ownership/constraints/team gap; standards and organizational foundations; Monday actions and team questions. It also predicts software-development studies, comparison tables, a direct practitioner tone and explicit limits on numerical inference. Those predictions match the frozen body. Its uncertainty about whether the linked reactor essay is required is resolved by the self-contained explanation in the article, not by an unannounced section.

The opening uses a specific, familiar adoption scenario—buying and distributing tools is expected to speed up the organization—then explains its appeal, states the competing thesis, and gives a roadmap. It is neither a generic placeholder, a restated question, a dictionary opening, a sweeping historical opening, nor a book report.

Closing Thought p47–p51 does not merely rephrase the thesis: it combines what to amplify with which stage to improve, states the consequence for people relying on the system, and hands off an already introduced ownership constraint. It does not open with a formulaic conclusion signal, delay the central thesis, introduce new study evidence, or replace reasoning with sentiment. Understanding generated work has already appeared in Cost p25 and Monday p44, so the final link is not a new subtopic.

The conclusion combines the task/input argument with the delivery-constraint argument: even a useful local effect must reach the people relying on the system. Its explicit alternative is more waiting work or maintenance, which supplies the practical consequence for allocating effort and budget. That combined decision—improve inputs and choose the constrained stage, then judge the delivered result—goes beyond any single evidence section.

The specified callback is explicit in Closing Thought ¶1: automatic gains and how hard to press return to the opening purchasing/pedal story. The paired amplify what and amplify which part questions then replace that story with choices about inputs and constraints, as the spec requires.

results.finding: Flow reader 2 reports this as out-of-place wording because it addresses the writer about attribution and hedging rather than helping the reader choose a resource. It interrupts the reference list’s otherwise clear reader-facing purpose; reader 1 does not report it. The source pointer identifies the corresponding evidence cluster because this reference apparatus has no paragraph-level spec entry.

The AC-1 reader explains dependence on goals, skills, codebase, standards, workflow and task fit; distinguishes the experienced-developer slowdown from separate junior-developer task gains; and rejects a universal ranking or performance formula. It names both limits required by the expected answer—new capability and task-varying gain—and says expertise or felt speed cannot guarantee benefit.

The AC-2 reader explains that extra generation reaches an unchanged review constraint, accumulates in a queue instead of releases, and creates more coordination and integration work for the already constrained people and systems. This recovers the expected non-bottleneck mechanism and explains increased downstream ownership effort alongside flat delivery. It also distinguishes felt from measured local gains. The answer does not separately restate long-term maintenance forecasts or the legacy example; its causal account of extra ownership work is sufficient for the stated outcome without requiring those particular examples.

The AC-3 reader proposes a representative pilot comparing work with and without AI, separately measures time, tasks, correctness, quality and effort/cost, follows review queues and delivery throughput/stability, and includes downstream maintenance. It would improve goals, context, tests, standards, review/ownership capacity and the actual limiting stage before expansion, use AI at that stage only after a measured trial, and assign accountability. This covers every element of the expected answer without inventing required rollout thresholds.
